title: Why Some City Blocks Run So Much Hotter
hook: The city itself is cooking your block.
closing: The redlining maps are gone. The heat still remembers them.
question: Does your neighborhood feel hotter than it should?

segments.say: Across major US cities, pavement and buildings add an average of 8 degrees of extra heat.
68 percent of everyone studied live in the very hottest, most paved-over city blocks.
Neighborhoods redlined back in the 1930s are, on average, 5 degrees hotter today than nearby areas that weren't.
